    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersMinted pea and feta toastsToasted baguette with smashed peas, mint, feta and lemonHow to make it1 baguette2 tbsp olive oil300g frozen peas1/4 cup mint leaves, chopped100g feta1 lemonsalt and pepper, to tasteSlice the baguette and brush with oil.Toast the slices under the grill or in a hot oven until golden.Cook the peas in boiling water until tender, then drain.Smash the peas with the mint, crumbled feta, a squeeze of lemon and salt and pepper to taste.Spread thickly on the toasts and run a fork along the top for crocodile ridges.Mermaid lagoon prawnsGreen prawns poached in lemon water, chilled in iced water, tails onHow to make it500g green prawns2 lemons1 tbsp salt1kg ice1/2 cup mayonnaise2 tbsp tomato sauce1 tsp hot sauceBring a pot of water to the boil with the salt and the lemon slices.Poach the prawns until pink.Plunge into iced water to stop the cooking.Peel the prawns, leaving the tails on.Mix the mayonnaise, tomato sauce, a squeeze of lemon and the hot sauce.Serve the prawns on ice with the sauce.Skull Rock gruyère and pepper puffsThe rock where Hook holds Tiger LilyHow to make itAs written, serves 4Golden choux puffs loaded with gruyère and cracked black pepper, crisp outside and hollow inside, served warm from the oven.Boil 250ml water with 100g butter and a pinch of salt, tip in 150g plain flour and beat over the heat for 1 minute until it leaves the sides.Cool 5 minutes, then beat in 4 eggs one at a time until glossy.Stir in 120g grated gruyère and 1 tsp cracked pepper.Pipe 30 small balls onto lined trays, top with a little extra cheese and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until puffed and golden.Johnny cakes with maple syrupTick tock. The croc wants seconds.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsCaptain Hook's beef and allspice stewBeef chuck stewed with allspice and molasses, no surprise package insideHow to make it1kg beef chuck, diced2 tbsp plain flour3 tbsp olive oil2 brown onions, sliced3 carrots, chopped1 tsp ground allspice1 tbsp molasses or brown sugar1 tbsp tomato paste750ml beef stock1 crusty loafsalt and pepper, to tasteToss the beef in the flour. Slice the onions and chop the carrots.Brown the beef in batches in the olive oil in a heavy pot.Soften the onions and carrots.Return the beef and add the allspice, molasses, tomato paste and stock.Cover and simmer gently until thick and tender.Season well with salt and pepper and serve in big bowls with crusty bread.Lost Boys' honey paprika drumsticksThe Lost Boys' hideout under the treeHow to make itAs written, serves 4Sticky drumsticks roasted in honey, paprika and garlic, with buttered corn cobs and crispy roast potatoes, all eaten with your hands.Toss 12 chicken drumsticks with 3 tbsp honey, 2 tsp smoked paprika, 3 crushed garlic cloves, 2 tbsp oil and salt.Roast at 200°C for 40 minutes, turning once, until sticky and cooked through.Roast 1kg potato chunks tossed in oil alongside for 45 minutes.Boil 4 corn cobs for 6 minutes, cut in half and roll in butter.Pile everything onto one big board.SweetsTinker Bell fairy breadButtered white bread covered in sprinkles, cut into triangles. Think a wonderful thought.How to make it12 slices of soft white bread80g butter, softened100g hundreds and thousands1 tsp edible glitterButter the bread right to the edges.Press each buttered side into a plate of hundreds and thousands until well covered.Cut into triangles.Dust with the edible glitter and pile on a plate.DrinksNana's bedtime malted vanilla milkWarm milk whisked with malt powder, honey and vanillaHow to make it1 L milk4 tbsp malted milk powder2 tbsp honey1 tsp vanilla extract100ml cream1 whole nutmeg8 plain biscuitsHeat the milk in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling.Off the heat, whisk in the malted milk powder, honey and vanilla until frothy.Whip the cream to soft peaks.Pour into mugs, spoon a little cream on each and grate over nutmeg. Serve with a plain biscuit.Lemon barley waterWendy pours it before the story starts.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
